The publication-disabled simulated-Actions build-core run and independent native-local build-core run reproduced the package, resolver metadata, and both ABI artifacts byte for byte. ARMHF logs are byte-identical. Parallel ARM64 output differs in complete-line ordering, but both current logs and both tracked historical oracles have the same line multiset and independently satisfy the exact fail-closed CrocoDS proof.

The pristine source is commit 87bbb3d9007ac537864278c6c3149ae3291873f8, tree 5a76585f521954c8e8ebef9b489a4d6c7a8b73db, with no submodules. The proof binds native leading-space version 87bbb3d to all 50 C compile commands per ABI, every source/object and ordered compiler invocation, the exact ordered link, and binary identity git 87bbb3d. ARM64 retains exactly nine reviewed warnings and seven notes across five ordered diagnostic streams; ARMHF is warning- and note-free.

Resolver metadata reports display_version v1, MIT licensing, DSK/SNA/KCR content, needs_kbd_mouse_focus=true, disk_control=false, and libretro_saves=false. CPC content loading, keyboard focus, controls, disk and tape behavior, audio and video pacing, savestates, frontend integration, compatibility, and sustained performance remain target-runtime gates.

The repository root license and resolver metadata say MIT, while compiled CrocoDS source headers state GPLv2-or-later and bundled zlib 1.1.3 carries separate notice terms. Compiled cpc6128.bin.c and romdisc.bin.c arrays contain no local license header or provenance record. The package carries neither corresponding source nor a license inventory, so any public distribution or release remains a human legal and policy gate even though the local bytes reproduce.

Both builds clone the exact source over the network; no offline source bundle or network-disabled rebuild is proven. The portable toolchain archives and loaded image identities are locked, but cached images retain dockerfile_linkage=unverified-local-cache as an explicit provenance limitation.

ARM64 requires GLIBC_2.17 and records the AArch64 loader and libc. ARMHF is EABI5 hard-float, reaches GLIBC_2.7, and records libc and libm. Provider compatibility is unverified. The portable artifacts bind only to ra64-universal-v1 and ra32-a30-v1; all device views remain ineligible pending provider and target-runtime evidence.
